title: Factory Pattern and SOLID
reported: Why and when to use the factory pattern (with code); the open/closed principle and how factory designs can violate it.

sources.passage:
My Arcesium SSE Interview Experience 

Recently, I interviewed for the Senior Software Engineer 2.2 year experience ,role at Arcesium. Although I didn’t make it through the final round, the process gave me a lot of learnings worth sharing.

🔹 Round 1: Online Test (HackerRank)

The journey started with a coding round on HackerRank, focused on DSA & problem-solving.

🔹 Round 2: Technical Interview

Solved the Koko Eating Bananas problem (Binary Search).

Deep dive into my resume projects.

Discussion around Kafka fundamentals and its real-world usage.

🔹 Round 3: Low Level Design (LLD)

Asked to design an Uber-like system.

Broke it down into core entities: User, Driver, Ride, Payment, Location, vehicle.

Emphasis on database normalization and scalability.

🔹 Round 4: Hiring Manager Round

This was a theory-heavy round testing depth of knowledge:

Database Indexing: Clustered vs Non-Clustered Index (with diagrams).

Design Patterns: Factory Pattern — why/when we need it + sample code.

SOLID Principles: Open/Closed Principle, failure cases & resolution strategiesin Factory Pattern .

❌ Outcome

I got rejected in the HM round. The feedback was clear:

“Your theoretical concepts need to be explained with more clarity, depth, and examples.”

🌱 Key Takeaways

Arcesium focuses heavily on core CS fundamentals — not just coding.

LLD should be backed with proper DB design & normalization.

Be ready to draw diagrams, write code snippets, and explain trade-offs in theory-heavy rounds.

Strong fundamentals (DBMS, Design Patterns, SOLID) matter as much as problem-solving.

Arcesium - Software Engineer Role(1+ years exp) - India

Interview 2 - Second interview was on OOPs, Design patterns, in-depth knowledge of C++ and Javascript because these are my preferred languages, Dbms, MongoDB, MySQL, and some discussions on what I have worked on in my previous company.

Interview 3 - Third interview was a Hiring manager round, where I was again asked design patterns, had to code one of the very famous patterns, some questions again were on my projects and the previous company work, and lastly to design and code a small problem. 

Interview 4 - Fourth interview was with the Hr, where we had a discussion on my work experience mainly..

All rounds went well.
Got the offer!

* An effective elevator pitch encapsulates your identity, professional background, and aspirations for your next role, setting the stage for a potential "Tell me about yourself" inquiry.
* An elevator pitch markets you as a confident potential hire. During the early stages of an interview process or even a networking event, elevator pitches can be particularly helpful because employers may be looking at a high volume of potential candidates or meeting a lot of people. Speaking convincingly about what you bring to the table can help immediately signal your professional skills!

## ****Interview Ends.****

I was notified that I had been selected, after 20 days.

****The final piece of advice:****

* The online test and both interviews were on an easy to moderate level.
* Keep your basics strong of Data Structure, OOPs, and SQL.
* The interviewer focuses on whatever written in the Resume, so try to be honest with it.
* Try to be confident and interacting during the interview. You can move the direction of the interview according to you.
* Do your research about the company. Like its history, what the company does, which technology it uses etc.

conducted online. The questions posed during the interview included:

* Introduce yourself briefly.
* Discuss your projects.
* Which programming language do you prefer among Python, SQL, and Shell Scripting? (I opted for Python)
* Distinguish between List and Tuple.
* Explain Decorator and Generator.
* Define Encapsulation.
* Explain the logic behind two code snippets: Factorial and Leap Year.
* Respond to SQL queries, including Primary Key, fetching unique values from a database, and syntax for deleting values from a table, among others.

Upon concluding the technical questions, the interviewer inquired if I had any questions for them. I seized the opportunity to inquire about the latest technologies Capgemini was working on and the technologies a fresher should focus on in the current market. Satisfied with my responses, the interviewer concluded the session.

****HR Interview****

Two days post the Technical Interview, I underwent the HR interview, also conducted online. This interview lasted approximately 10–15 minutes, with questions as follows:

* Introduce yourself.
* Inquire about my current city and any location preferences.
* Discuss my foreign language hobby mentioned in my resume, including which language I am proficient in and my practice regimen.
* Explore my future plans.
* Inquire about family members in the IT sector, if any, and their associated companies.
* Discuss my technical skills and my preferred technologies for work.
* Towards the end of the interview, the interviewer invited any questions from my end before concluding the session.
